feeds.title: Byzantine Tales Blog
feeds.description: A site dedicated to the creation of graphic novels and comic books about the medieval world, the Byzantine Empire, and Greek history. Byzantine Tales was created in 2019, when we decided to combine our passion for art and history to create a series of illustrated books that focus on stories from Greek and Roman history. Our vision is to bring to life the history of the quite unknown medieval Roman East.

feeds.title: Ikonographics Blog
feeds.description: Julia Bridget Hayes was born in South Africa and lives in Athens, Greece. She studied photography for a year at the Pretoria Technikon before coming to Greece in 1998 to study Theology at the Social Theology Faculty of the University of Athens on a scholarship. Explore her Ikonographics tutorials, step-by-step guides in the blog.

feeds.title: Oxford University Byzantine Society
feeds.description: The Oxford University Byzantine Society (OUBS) is a graduate student run organisation which provides support and information for graduate students of Late Antique and Byzantine Studies (LABS) and adjacent disciplines at Oxford University. It also provides opportunities for graduate students to present their work to their peers from institutions across the globe and acts as a hub for the sharing of information about job opportunities, studentships, funding, conferences, and seminars as well as publications and resources.

feeds.title: St. Mary Byzantine Catholic Church Blog
feeds.description: We are a parish of the Holy Protection of Mary Byzantine Catholic Eparchy of Phoenix. Explore our blog to know more about our faith, church events, news and more!

feeds.title: Konstantia Kaloethina
feeds.description: Konstantia Kaloethina came to the kingdom of Calontir in 2005, after a few years of hearing about this magnificent historical world called the Society for Creative Anachronism. They are proteged to Master Gabriel andvaka Kjotvason. Explore the arts and byzantine stories in the blog.

feeds.title: Byzantine Catholic Church In America
feeds.description: Information on Byzantine Christian faith and worship. Includes directories, news, calendars, message boards, and links to other Orthodox and Catholic Churches. ByzCath.org is an unofficial site developed and maintained by volunteers that supports, but is not connected to the official Church. We strive to provide accurate news and information about the Byzantine Catholic and other Eastern Christian Churches.

feeds.title: Christ The Bridegroom
feeds.description: Founded in 2009, we are a Byzantine Catholic women's monastery in the Eparchy of Parma, living in and drawing others into the spousal love of Christ through prayer and hospitality. Get the latest updates on our life and daily events, happening in the church and Monastery in our blog.

feeds.title: St. Philip Byzantine Catholic Church
feeds.description: We are a Catholic parish of the Byzantine Ruthenian tradition. We are in full communion with Pope Francis. We belong to the Byzantine Catholic Holy Protection of Mary Eparchy of Phoenix, under the leadership of Bishop Thomas Olmstead. Stay up to date with all the news on Parish, church, sermons and more with our bulletins.

feeds.title: Byztex Blog
feeds.description: Discussions of Eastern Christianity, often with a Byzantine flavor. Posts on the Oriental Orthodox, Eastern Orthodox, Eastern Catholic, and even the occasional church of the West.

feeds.title: Byzantine Emporia
feeds.description: The Byzantine Emporia blog exists to provide more information about products on byzantinemporia.com and to share those interests that inspired this site. The idea for Byzantine Emporia came from my love of travel and history. It always fascinated me what a single item could tell you about the history and culture of the people who made it. Here we explore that background a bit more. We discuss the history and geography that define cultures the world over, and how those cultures in turn adapt by creating objects that are both beautiful and practical.

feeds.title: Byzantine Real History
feeds.description: Byzantine Real History is an online source focusing and researching the magnificent Byzantine history and a project which strives for a serous discussion focused on the history of the Roman Empire during the Byzantine era (330-1453 AD). It's goal is to dismantle stereotypes formed around 'Byzantium' by ignoramous historians.

feeds.title: Anna's New Rome
feeds.description: Magistrissa Anna Dokeianina Syrakousina came to the Barony of the Bridge in the East Kingdom by ways of Trimaris in 2002, where she had been playing on and off for a few years during high school and college. She is painfully obsessed with all things Greek, Roman, and Eastern Roman/Medieval Greek (Byzantine), and enjoys blabbing about her recent projects and teaching classes. Explore all her stories and learnings in this blog.

feeds.title: Byzantine Military Blog
feeds.description: Byzantine Military Blog is dedicated to the military history and civilization of the Eastern Roman Empire (330 to 1453).

feeds.title: The Byzantine Life » Byzantine
feeds.description: The Byzantine Life is a blog about bringing an Eastern flair to Catholic living and give organizing consultations. My Byzantine name is Kyleshka, and I am a God-fearing, homeschooling, writer, wife, and mom.

feeds.title: The Byzantium Blogger Blog
feeds.description: A collection of art and military history of the Byzantium empire. This site aims to tell the story of the fascinating and complex history of the Byzantine Empire through various posts whether they are narrative stories, lists of interesting facts about the empire and its history, or interviews with other enthusiasts of the subject matter. Our goal is to present the fascinating history of Byzantium in a fun yet smart way to prove that Byzantium and its history is something not only something that interests scholars and historians but everyday people.

feeds.title: The Based Byzantine Blog
feeds.description: Welcome to my blog, The Based Byzantine, where I discuss topics related to Eastern Christianity, the interface between the Latin and Greek Churches, and the reunion of Slavic Christendom in the Universal Church under Rome. I am DJ (Daniel) Shulick. I have a passion for learning, discussing, and writing about ancient Christian (Catholic and Orthodox) subjects, playing and composing secular and sacred music in classical styles, and enjoying God's creation.

feeds.title: Byzantine Philosophy Blog
feeds.description: Welcome to the official blog of the International Network for Byzantine Philosophy. Here you will find short communications, reflections, and announcements of events and publications related to the field of Byzantine Philosophy. The initiative for the International Network for Byzantine Philosophy has arisen from the increasing body of published texts and studies in Byzantine philosophy. It is only in the last twenty years or so that we have seen growth in this field of Byzantine studies following the pioneering work of Basil Tatakis (1896-1996) and Linos Benakis (b. 1928-).

feeds.title: St. Michael's Byzantine
feeds.description: St. Michael the Archangel Byzantine Catholic Church is a catholic church of the Byzantine rite. Follow all the latest coverage from the church on the site along ith articles on faith and humanity.

feeds.title: The Nordic Byzantine Network
feeds.description: The Nordic Byzantine Network (NBN) was the outcome of a three-week seminar at the Swedish institutes of Istanbul, Athens and Rome. The collected impressions from a number of excursions and lectures at the Mediterranean inspired the participating scholars to establish the network of cooperation. On this page we have saved some of the essays, book reviews, seminar and conference reports and other things that were previously posted on the old website.

feeds.title: After Constantine Blog
feeds.description: 'After Constantine' is a peer-reviewed and open-access academic journal and it is published online once a year. Its purpose is to bring Late Antiquity to the spotlight by hosting papers that underline its importance to classic and byzantine studies and contribute to a better piece of knowledge in the academic community. Our journal encourages the ecumenical dialogue between historical, archaeological, and theological subjects around the Late Antique and Early Byzantine period, especially in the East.

feeds.title: Mr Bello Blog » Byzantine
feeds.description: Learn more about the byzantine era with the articles reviewing historical articles on byzantine warriors and events.
